audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 fits 52.37% over 655 games: Zoe's only defensive tool in lane is a one-second Portal Jump, so every stage belongs to Irelia provided Sleepy Trouble Bubble is dodged.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike named Trinity/Black Cleaver against report[8]'s on-hit build, and no field carried Portal Jump's real cooldown.
audit.why: Portal Jump is 11s at rank 1 and 5s at rank 3 — it is not a once-a-fight escape, and that changes how many commits she can refuse.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] rewritten to the first item generally with her 800 range and the 18-second bubble gap; Portal Jump's cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer called her hop 'E' in early, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1]. E is Sleepy Trouble Bubble; the blink is Portal Jump (R). The sleep's actual payload — reduced Magic Resist and the first damage that breaks it being doubled — was never stated.
audit.why: A reader told to punish 'after her E hop' will step into the bubble instead, and the doubled wake-up hit is the reason a landed sleep kills.
audit.corrected: All three fields corrected to Portal Jump; the MR cut and doubled wake-up damage written into breakdown.cooldowns and enemyWin.
sources: packet defects — never names any Zoe ability

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18s to 14s; Portal Jump 11s to 5s.

edits.before: - Zoe Sleepy Trouble Bubble: matchup-defining — Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sleepy Trouble Bubble (E) is 18s at rank 1 and 14s at rank 5 — asleep, your MR is cut and the first hit that wakes you is doubled, so body-block the bubble with minions or terrain. - Portal Jump (R) is 11s at rank 1 and 5s at rank 3: she can blink out of one commit every fight.

edits.before: Zoe wins by landing Sleepy Trouble Bubble, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Zoe wins by sleeping you, doubling the hit that wakes you, and blinking out with Portal Jump when you answer.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by respecting one cooldown: dodge the 18-second bubble and she has nothing left to stop a reset chain.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Zoe's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, deny her the sightline: bubble needs a clean line, so approach along terrain and she has no opener at all.

edits.before: You control this lane from level 1 through 6 since Zoe has no way to survive extended melee range once your Q dash lands, and her only real deterrent is landing sleep bubble on you before you close. Approach along terrain or through minions to break her bubble's line, and punish her aggressively any time she uses Q or W to poke since her follow-up mobility (E hop) barely creates distance. Her base stats are low enough that even a partial trade often wins outright at level 3 if her bubble whiffs. Respect her all-in potential only in the brief window right after she lands a clean sleep, since her burst combo into a sleeping target is significant.
edits.after: You control this lane from level 1 through 6 since Zoe has no way to survive extended melee range once your Q dash lands, and her only real deterrent is landing sleep bubble on you before you close. Approach along terrain or through minions to break her bubble's line, and punish her any time she spends Paddle Star to poke, since Portal Jump only blinks her out for one second. Her base stats are low enough that even a partial trade often wins outright at level 3 if her bubble whiffs. Respect her all-in potential only in the brief window right after she lands a clean sleep, since her burst combo into a sleeping target is significant.

edits.before: Punish her low mobility immediately after she uses a spell shot to poke, since her E only offers minor repositioning
edits.after: Punish her low mobility right after she spends Paddle Star, since Portal Jump only blinks her away for one second

edits.before: Use E to hop over terrain and disengage or reposition for poke angles

edits.before: Once you have Trinity/Black Cleaver your dash speed and burst outscale her long-range poke pattern, letting you close before she can land a second bubble.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, your dash speed and burst outscale her 800-range poke, letting you close inside the 18-second gap between bubbles.

notes: Two MISGENDER findings are deliberately NOT fixed here: report[3].t and report[11].t. The brief caps report[] rewrites at two per matchup and report[0].t and report[1].t were used for the two most visible ones; report[3].t ('onto his chest ... he budgeted zero for') and report[11].t ('Trade at his range between waves') still call Zoe he/his and need a separate pass. The kit file flags Sleepy Trouble Bubble as trueDamage; Riot's description says only that sleep reduces Magic Resist and doubles the first damage that breaks it, so no true-damage or resistance-bypass claim was written.
